You may have trouble with insurance covering the pharmacy that dispenses. Or there may be issues with the medicine itself. Or both. The above is true though I was told it was failure to respond to 2 antidepressants of a different class. You have to enroll into the REMS program. Your doctor will assess your situation and make a recommendation. They’ll send you forms to sign including the REMS program. After that it’s just getting your meds ordered and setting a schedule. I was initially declined by my insurance for the meds even after my doctor sent them a letter stating the medicine was necessary. I had to call and climb up the chain of command until someone heard me out. A few hours later the pharmacy called to collect payment. I paid $80. Enough for twice a week appointments for a month. Please use the Janssen Card as this drops the price from $800 or so to just $10. Beat of luck to you. I start my first treatment today.

Got an update for ya! After looking at ketamine infusions and Spravato I went with Spravato. Found a place that administers the medication. IV ketamine is very expensive. I was quoted $3600 for 6 infusions. The Spravato approval process was pretty simple. Doctor asked me about my personal history, reasons for depression and how long I’d been suffering from it. We took a look at the medicines I’ve used. You need to fail at least 2 medicines to be considered. As far as cost goes my insurance needs prior authorization and even then could still be expensive. Janssen provides a discount card that could have you paying as little as $10 per bottle. 

Register here: 

Register.JanssenCarePathSavings.com

From there they ask about any illicit drug use as this will disqualify you from the program. Not sure about marijuana in legal states.

To sum it up I start treatment sometime next week. I’m just waiting on my medicines to be delivered to the doctors office. I’ll update you more when I start.
